notes: Six own pages read, all HTTP 200 and not thin (home via https://fieldpulse.com/, pricing, the AI info page, company, partners, and the cited own plumbing guide). The pricing page's FAQ shows questions only (answers are collapsed and not in the text), so seat types and contract terms (C03, C04) are unverifiable. C07 (flat-rate or flat monthly pricing with no per-user fees) is wrong against the pricing page's seat-based statement. Cause trace for C07 read four pages cited by both answers: the FieldPulse plumbing blog (no such statement), clientility.com (does not mention FieldPulse), workyard.com (calls FieldPulse per-seat) and closecrew.ai (gives the flat monthly, no per-user fee model to Service Fusion, not FieldPulse); no cited page carries the claim about FieldPulse, so the cause is not found. For the reviewer: the answers' wording matches closecrew's Service Fusion entry, which suggests a misattribution, but that is not recorded as a cause. Comparative lines (pricing does not penalize growth as aggressively as competitors) and the G2 rating were not coded. Team-size ranges (5 to 200+ employees, 7 to 50 techs) are positioning, not customer counts. No dollar price is published, so C09 is unverifiable. Pass 2 (8 Oct 2026): no browser reads exist for this vendor and no claim was unverifiable because of a blocked page. The gap lines and every table and sub-heading section were checked; the in-scope statements found there (custom or seat-based pricing, QuickBooks, mobile app, founding year and Dallas) were already instances of existing claims, so nothing was added. Consistency check: C07 (flat-rate pricing with no per-user fees) stays wrong, because the pricing page states that FieldPulse is seat-based, the same pricing basis.
